claims.claim: The proposal requests 420,000 ADA plus a 105,000 ADA contingency reserve, with a 15,750 ADA Intersect administration fee, totaling 540,750 ADA.
The requested funding covers a part-time maintainer for UTxO RPC over 12 months at an annual rate of $105,000 USD.
UTxO RPC is an open interface specification that standardizes interactions with UTxO-based blockchains using Protocol Buffers and SDKs in Rust, Go, Node.js, .NET, Haskell, and Python.
The document states that UTxO RPC has been adopted by Amaru, Dingo, and the Haskell Cardano node as a query interface.
The project maintains more than 10 repositories covering the core specification, language SDKs, documentation, and provider integrations, and is open-source under Apache 2.0.
The proposal states that it achieved the required 67% support threshold in the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The document claims the withdrawal does not breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission.

Intersect will administer funds through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with TRSC and PSSC addresses, role-based authorization thresholds, external oversight entities, milestone-based disbursement controls, and a public dashboard.
TxPipe has received funding through 30 Project Catalyst proposals from Funds 9 through 14, with 26 delivered and 4 under development and on schedule.
TxPipe received 2025 Intersect open-source maintenance funding for Pallas, Dolos, and UTxO RPC, and the document states all are being delivered on schedule.

summary: The document requests 540,750 ADA for a 12-month UTxO RPC maintenance grant administered by Intersect, with stated work on specification maintenance, SDK upkeep, community support, and AI-oriented documentation, plus governance claims about Hydra voting support, NCL compliance, and smart-contract-based oversight.
